_comment: Personal pronouns drawn as a picture, not searched for and not clozed (tunatale-3rxu, the user 2026-09-28). Each maps a word to a language-neutral concept in app.cards.pronoun_scenes.PRONOUN_CONCEPTS; the picture is a conversation with the referent filled and standing outside the outline, because a pronoun's meaning IS a relation between people and a photo cannot carry one. A word listed here is NOT a function word, whatever `function_words.json` or a POS tag says: app.srs.function_words.is_function_word vetoes it, so a PRON never goes down the case-marker cloze route. The veto is asked about a bare token, so listing a homograph would take EVERY sense of it off the picture route — the picture is therefore only drawn when the card's English gloss names the referent (app.cards.pronoun_picture.gloss_matches). Map only words whose MAIN sense is the personal pronoun. `kita` is also the root of 'to see' and of `kitaon` ('let's'), which is the one live homograph in this file: the token veto would have taken every sense of it off the picture route, so it is listed and the GLOSS guard does the separating instead — a `kita` glossed 'see' gets no picture. `siya` maps to third_one and carries NO gender mark. `kita` is the inclusive we and `kami` the exclusive one, the same distinction Tagalog draws. The `_poss` words are the FREE FORMS of the possessive (tunatale-uy38): the same conversation scene as their nominative, with a bag carried by every lit referent, which is what keeps `siya` ('he/she') and `niya` ('his/her') two different words on two different pictures. `ko` ('his/her') and `mo` ('my/our') are NOT here on purpose, and neither is `ka` ('your/yours'): each is an enclitic whose free form above already carries the same meaning, so the enclitic is drilled as a cloze and the free form gets the picture — listing both would put one meaning on two pictures and take the enclitic off the cloze route and back on again. `ka` is additionally in `function_words.json`'s include list, where a listing would be dead data. `niya` is the gender-neutral 'his/her' and takes the third_one_poss picture, which is the only place the possessive says which referent it is: the gloss decides, since the scene is the same for all of them. `ta` IS listed although it is the enclitic of `kita`, the exception to the rule above: in the user's deck `kita` is glossed 'see' and so gets no picture, which left `ta` as the only card for the inclusive we (the user, 2026-09-29). `mi`, the enclitic of `kami`, is listed too (the user, 2026-10-14: "Why does mi not have an svg?"): its card was minted with a Pixabay photo of 'we', and it shares kami's exclusive-we picture as `ta` shares kita's. Whether enclitic pronouns should be clozes instead is an open question on the short-forms decisions bead (tunatale-7jl1). Its gloss must still name the referent ('we') for the picture to be drawn. `glosses` (2026-10-14, tunatale-jm3d): the card gloss for a listed word, written by the pronoun table rather than the lesson's in-context gloss, which reached the deck as 'we' for kami/mi/ta and 'you (singular)' for nimo. Per language because Cebuano's genitive is also the agent ('by me'), which a language-neutral label would put on Slovene 'moj' too. `kita` has none: it is also 'see'.

glosses.niya: his / her; by him or her
